text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- An over-the-counter market went on line on Friday trading the mass privatisation shares of six companies.
- Iran plans to pay back its outstanding debts to Romania amounting to some $50 million in oil products deliveries until the end of January 1997.
LIBERTATEA

- The policies pursued by Prime Minister's Nicolae Vacaroiu's government compelled the central bank to give 3.7 trillion leu to agriculture and 250 billion lei to troubled bank Renasterea Creditului Romanesc Credfit Bank SA and Banca Dacia Felix SA, the newspaper says.
- European Investment Bank gave Romania a loan worth 70 million Ecus to upgrade its road network.
VOCEA ROMANIEI
- Russia will deliver some 150 million cubic metres of gas to Romania to pay its outstanding debt worth $12 million.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) bloc is to hold a rally on Thursday, the last day of campaigning ahead of November 3 parliamentary and presidential elections.
- The newspaper publishes the CDR "Contract with Young People", a 12-point programme urging young people to vote.
- Remus Opris, the CDR's campaign manager, asks voters not to be discouraged by what he calles the "falsified" opinion polls published by the ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR).
ADEVARUL
- The newspaper publishes the transcript of the debate held by the newspaper with nine of the 16 presidential candidates.

- In the race for the presidency, President Ion Iliescu leads with 36.5 percent followed by Emil Constantinescu with 24.7 percent, says an opinion poll by the independent IMAS. In the parliamentary polls, the CDR, with 32.7 percent, is ahead of the ruling PDSR with 31.2 percent.
- State television is holding a four-hour debate with all 16 presidential candidates on Thursday starting 1900 local.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- "Huge electoral fraud is being plotted" reads the headline of an editorial commenting on what it says is total control by the ruling PDSR over administration, television, state institutions and the central electoral bureau.

In a full-page report, the daily says Iliescu and the ruling PDSR are preparing even more elaborate ways of cheating in the election than in 1946, when the communists reversed the results of elections to take power.

- Romania's leading Communist-era dissident, Doina Cornea, urges Romanians to vote for one of the opposition parties -- the CDR, Social Democratic Union (USD) or National Liberal Alliance -- to put an end to the "Iliescu regime".
JURNALUL NATIONAL
- President Iliescu says in an interview that any coalition between the three major parties -- PDSR, CDR and USD -- is possible after the polls.
ZIUA
- Leading politicians describe as an attempt at intimidation the jailing by a Bucharest court of two of the daily's journalists on charges of defaming President Iliescu.
LIBERTATEA
- A crude bomb placed in a restaurant owned by a Turkish citizen injured six people, says the newspaper in a report alleging that mafia-like bomb attacks have come to Romania.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The newspaper publishes proposals by the three main presidential contenders -- Iliescu, Constantinescu and USD candidate Petre Roman -- to fight corruption.
- Leading analyst Dorel Sandor says the very creation of the next government will be a huge problem in itself before it can even tackle the difficulties facing it.
- The newspaper publishes the PDSR's electoral programme.
VOCEA ROMANIEI

- An opinion poll by the independent ANSOP shows Iliescu leading with 32 percent support and his PDSR losing Bucharest and other major towns to the CDR, but leading in villages. ($=3,327 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
